episode_title: From Upwork to 100-Person Consultancy: How Subscriptions Fueled Growth | Taylor Hersom

real_qa.q: How did Taylor Hersom grow Eden Data Consultancy from Upwork freelancing to a 100-person firm by 2025?
real_qa.r: Taylor started on Upwork in 2020 after quitting his Chief Security Officer role, gamifying the platform by offering cheap rates for five-star reviews, then gradually raising rates. He tested a subscription model on Upwork that proved popular, leading him to formally establish Eden Data in 2021. By 2025, the company had scaled to nearly 100 employees through bootstrapped growth, focusing on culture, employee satisfaction, and a subscription-based pricing model for ongoing compliance services.
real_qa.requete: Taylor Hersom Eden Data Consultancy growth Upwork

real_qa.q: Why did Eden Data Consultancy adopt a subscription model instead of hourly billing for compliance consulting?
real_qa.r: Taylor implemented subscriptions initially for predictability and easier revenue tracking as he scaled his team. On Upwork, he offered subscriptions as an alternative to hourly rates and found that clients overwhelmingly preferred them. The subscription model worked because compliance services are indefinite—clients need ongoing management, audits, and regulatory updates every month indefinitely, making recurring revenue more natural than project-based billing.
real_qa.requete: subscription model compliance consulting vs hourly

real_qa.q: What were the key challenges Taylor Hersom faced scaling Eden Data Consultancy from a solo consultant to 100 employees?
real_qa.r: Major scaling challenges included building HR infrastructure and ensuring compliance with employment law, tracking utilization and profitability per employee, managing multiple security frameworks and frameworks as new ones emerged, and maintaining consistent service delivery across a large team. Taylor had to build comprehensive training frameworks and adapt to the agile nature of the security industry with new frameworks constantly appearing.

real_qa.q: How did Eden Data Consultancy differentiate itself from traditional security consulting firms?
real_qa.r: Rather than selling a virtual CISO, Eden Data positioned itself as an external security and compliance team, ensuring customers interacted with multiple team members at different levels rather than a single siloed consultant. This provided continuity when team members took vacation or left. Additionally, the company invested heavily in branding and marketing, using neon colors and phrases like 'guard your privates' instead of the conventional blues, grays, and stock photography used by firms like Deloitte.
real_qa.requete: Eden Data Consultancy differentiation external team model

real_qa.q: What KPIs did Taylor Hersom use to measure success at Eden Data Consultancy?
real_qa.r: Taylor tracked customer satisfaction through personal monthly check-ins with clients and tied that feedback to employee performance. He monitored traditional metrics like gross margin and EBITDA, and most critically, revenue per headcount since labor costs were the primary expense. He also bonded employees based on revenue they generated, and measured utilization without requiring hour-by-hour tracking—instead breaking down time by customer and revenue.
real_qa.requete: consulting firm KPIs revenue per employee

guest.bio_context: Taylor Hersom founded Eden Data Consultancy, a compliance consulting firm providing SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, and other compliance services. He started as a freelancer on Upwork in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic after leaving his role as Chief Security Officer at a consulting firm. He scaled Eden Data from a solo operation to approximately 100 employees by 2025, when River Own acquired the company, and he transitioned to Managing Director at River Own.
